system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager

T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of experience in infrastructure,
including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Hands-on experience designing, building and
operating cloud environments, with strong Terraform experience. Builds self-service infrastructure and
observable, reliable platforms that help product teams deploy and operate services effectively.
CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront),
Terraform, Atlantis, Kubernetes, Linux
Platform engineering: Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and
error budgets, incident management
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, Puppet
Testing and operations: k6, on-call operations, capacity planning
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd Apr 2022 – present
Manchester / remote
• Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform spanning eight
clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane-based
self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced the time for a new service to reach
production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
• Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per week
by approximately 60%.
• Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
• Serve in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
Leeds
• Operated AWS game backend infrastructure (EC2, ECS and later EKS) for titles with up to 1.2
million daily active players.
• Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules, using Atlantis for
plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
• Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability
stack.
• Ran k6 load tests and launch-day capacity planning ahead of game launches.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
Sheffield
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration
management.
• Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer
incidents.
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023
LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. I bring 10 years of
infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a
strong record of designing and building infrastructure that helps product teams deploy and run
services reliably. Corvale’s engineering-led approach and the opportunity to help shape a new
train-to-cloud platform from its early architecture through to production particularly appeal to
me.
In my current role as Senior Platform Engineer at Tallybrook, I am technical lead for a
five-person team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters, around 350 services and
three regions. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD GitOps
and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3, reducing the time for a new
service to reach production from around two weeks to under one day. This work has involved
turning platform needs into practical infrastructure and supporting developers with services that
are easier to deploy and operate.
I also bring hands-on infrastructure-as-code and reliability experience relevant to Corvale’s scope.
At Brightwater Games, I managed AWS infrastructure through approximately 40 Terraform
modules, with Atlantis workflows for plan and apply on pull requests, and supported backend
systems serving titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players. Across my roles, I have
improved observability, introduced SLOs and error budgets, planned capacity, and contributed to
incident response. As incident commander in rotation and technical lead, I am accustomed to
taking ownership of technical work and helping teams deliver operationally sound systems.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my AWS platform, Terraform and operational
experience could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work and its end-to-end ownership of
technology. Thank you for your consideration.
Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
